study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate whether the person-based similarity index (PBSI) of sulcal width (SW) can identify a subgroup of schizophrenia patients with distinct cognitive and neurodevelopmental characteristics.

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: From a large longitudinal sample of patients with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-70 years (at baseline), we included individuals who had T1-weighted MRI scan acquisitions at 2 time points. Detailed information regarding diagnostic criteria and clinical assessments of the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis consortium are described in 29-31.

caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: Then, we applied a threshold, |PBSI-SW-Z| >2 (as in 34), to identify individuals whose morphometric profile is markedly dissimilar (at any time point) to the morphometric profiles of the normative group: the outliers.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Comparison of clinical, cognitive, and morphological characteristics (age, sex, PANSS scores, illness duration, estimated IQ, sulcation index) between outlier and non-outlier patient groups using t-tests and non-parametric permutation testing.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: A subgroup of schizophrenia patients with markedly deviant PBSI-SW showed extreme deficits in cognitive performance and cortical sulcation.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Significant deviance of PBSI-SW was present in a small group of patients (19 out of 164). These patients had significantly lower estimated IQ (p < .01) and a lower sulcation index (p = .03) compared to non-deviating patients. The progressive reduction of PBSI-SW in the schizophrenia group was driven by these deviating individuals.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study proposes that the PBSI-SW can be used for neuroimaging-driven subtyping of patients, which may help in identifying more biologically homogeneous subgroups within schizophrenia.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The small proportion of patients with considerable deviance in PBSI-SW led to small sample sizes for the clinical and cognitive characterization. IQ was estimated from subtests, not a full-scale score. Information about development or premorbid adjustment was not available.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study also calculated PBSI for cortical thickness (PBSI-CT) for comparison, but this metric did not show the same associations with clinical variables.
